what_it_does: This paper targets Vision Transformers — a class of AI model that processes images by dividing them into small patches and then computing how every patch relates to every other patch (a step called self-attention). The problem is that this comparison step grows quadratically: double the number of patches and the work quadruples, making large images expensive on GPUs. A known mitigation is token pruning — discarding patches that are judged unimportant — but the paper argues that existing methods ignore a finer-grained opportunity: even among the numbers that remain, many bits (the individual 0s and 1s that encode each number) are zero and can be skipped. SynGPU introduces an algorithm called Inter-token Bit-sparsity Awareness that identifies these skippable zero bits across similar patches and a hardware pathway called Bit-Serial Tensor Core (BSTC) that processes numbers one bit at a time through the GPU's math units, so zero bits cost almost nothing. It also defines a data layout (how numbers are arranged in memory) that lets standard GPU parallelism and the new bit-serial path work together rather than conflict. The result is claimed to accelerate Vision Transformer inference, though exact figures are not available from the abstract.
